paragraphs: Masabi sells fare payment technology to public transport agencies through a platform called Justride. Its account-based approach lets a passenger travel with a mobile phone, a contactless bank card or a smartcard.

The platform covers smart card, open payment, mobile ticketing, barcode and mobility-as-a-service through a suite of APIs and SDKs. A ready-to-go version arrives pre-integrated with validators, apps, payment gateways and acquiring banks. An open architecture with APIs, SDKs and pre-integrations is meant to make the system easier to implement and operate. The company says the platform is cloud-native and designed to scale for large cities and complex transit systems.

Masabi traces its start to launching the first UK mobile ticketing application with Chiltern Railways in 2007. It says it launched the first mobile ticketing deployment for a United States transit agency in 2012. The about page lists a London office address. It also lists addresses in Denver, Colorado, and in Cluj-Napoca, Romania.

quote.text: Quicker to launch, lower total cost of ownership, reduced risk, and continuous updates.
